question: Within the same ordinal silvering category (FIII, FIV, FV), where does capture condition add held-out discrimination of migration initiation?
training: Exactly the nested activation model coefficients from analysis/36; train on five of six projects, score the completely held-out project, using original nine-fish expert correction and outcome-free morphometric preprocessing.
primary: For each stage, pair-weighted within-project-year initiator/non-initiator concordance difference: score with Durif+length+timing+condition minus Durif+length+timing.
secondary: per-stage stage+condition versus stage alone, where stage-only AUC necessarily 0.5
informative project-year groups, positive and negative outcome counts, informative project coverage and pair counts
project-specific stage deltas and leave-one-project-out stage deltas
exploratory contrasts FIII minus FV and FIII minus FIV
uncertainty: 10000 deterministic project-level bootstrap resamples of six projects preserving per-project stage statistics; do not treat fish pairs as independent experimental units or infer causal mechanisms.
claim_rules: Show sample size, positive and negative cases, within-stage informative project coverage and interval before discussing stage trend.
When per-stage model overlap or support is sparse, do not promote an effect.
Stage differences were designed after overall AUC result and are exploratory; do not call pre-registered.
Inconsistent project-level signs prevent a general biological inference, even if pooled effects are positive.
Do not treat condition residual as independent physiology nor link it causally to reserves, hydraulic gates or escapement success.
